front.title: Interoperable Execution-Finality Authority Across Heterogeneous Computing Platforms: Protected Effect Semantics, Cross-Device Authority Continuity, and Resource-Side Enforcement

abstract.t: Computation is not authority to act. An operating system may authenticate an application, a device may recognize a permission, a cloud service may accept a token, an AI agent may hold a tool credential and a remote application may receive a command, yet none of these facts shows that the consequential operation actually executed is still within the originating authority, scope, current policy and resource state. This document describes an informational architecture for preserving an equivalent protected authorization relationship across heterogeneous platforms such as Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, cloud services, trusted hardware, edge devices and autonomous agents, whose native permission models and enforcement mechanisms differ. Qualified native evidence is translated into a protected canonical effect descriptor, scoped non-bearer enablement is created, and a receiving Finality Sink reconstructs the actual pending operation and enforces authority at a covered boundary. The document covers enforcement-capability qualification, cross-device ownership with source fencing, receipt-gated continuation, protected reauthorization, recovery and an honest account of what each mechanism can and cannot control.
